messages.content: What is the purpose of __init__ in Python classes?
The __init__ method is the constructor that initializes a new instance of a class. It's called automatically when you create an object and typically sets up instance attributes.
What does self represent?
self is a reference to the instance of the class, allowing you to access its attributes and methods. By convention, it's always the first parameter in instance methods.
Explain instance vs class attributes.
Instance attributes differ per object and are defined in __init__. Class attributes are shared across all instances and defined at the class level.
How do you access class vs instance attributes?
Access instance attributes via self.attr or obj.attr. Access class attributes via ClassName.attr or self.__class__.attr.
What happens with attribute shadowing?
An instance attribute with the same name as a class attribute hides the class attribute during lookup.
Can you have multiple __init__ methods?
No, only one __init__. Use @classmethod factory methods for alternative constructors.
What is name mangling?
Using double underscore prefix (e.g., __attr) makes attributes private by name mangling.
How do you prevent attribute modification?
Use @property with no setter or name mangling with double underscores.
What is the purpose of __slots__?
__slots__ restricts attributes an instance can have, reducing memory usage.
How much memory does __slots__ save?
For small classes, typically 40-50% by eliminating __dict__.
Can you add dynamic attributes with __slots__?
No, you're restricted to only defined slots.
How do you use __slots__ with inheritance?
Each class defines its own __slots__ for unique attributes.
What is the __dict__ attribute?
__dict__ stores instance attributes as a dictionary.
Can you access __dict__ with __slots__?
No, __slots__ removes __dict__ entirely.
How do class variables affect memory?
Class variables are shared, using less memory than instance variables for large numbers of objects.
How do you count instances of a class?
Use a class variable incremented in __init__ and decremented in __del__.
What is the purpose of using self in methods?
self allows each instance to access its own attributes and methods.
How do you define read-only class attributes?
Define at class level outside __init__, or use @property with no setter.
Can you shadow a class attribute in __init__?
Yes, assigning to self.attr creates an instance attribute that shadows the class attribute.
What is attribute lookup order?
Python checks instance __dict__ first, then class __dict__, then parent classes via MRO.
What is inheritance?
Inheritance allows a child class to inherit attributes and methods from a parent class.
What is the purpose of super()?
super() allows you to call methods from the parent class without duplicating code.
How do you override a method?
Define a method with the same name in the child class. Python uses the child's version.
What is Method Resolution Order (MRO)?
MRO is the order Python searches for methods in a class hierarchy using C3 linearization.
How do you check if a class is a subclass?
Use issubclass(ChildClass, ParentClass).
Can super() work without explicit parent?
Yes, in Python 3, super() without arguments automatically uses the enclosing class and self.
What is __bases__?
__bases__ is a tuple of direct parent classes.
What is __mro__?
__mro__ is the complete method resolution order tuple including all ancestors.
How do you view MRO?
Use Class.mro() or Class.__mro__.
What is the diamond problem?
A class inherits from two parents sharing a common ancestor, creating ambiguity.
How does Python solve diamond problem?
Using C3 linearization algorithm in MRO.
Can you skip a parent in MRO?
Not directly, but super() follows MRO in order.
How do you call a specific parent method?
Use ParentClass.method(self) to bypass MRO, or super() to follow it.
What happens if __init__ isn't called in a child?
Parent attributes won't be initialized, potentially causing AttributeErrors.
How do you access parent attributes?
Call super().__init__() in the child's __init__.
Can a child have different __init__ signature?
Yes, but call super().__init__() to initialize parent attributes.
What is abstract inheritance?
Defining an interface that subclasses must implement using abc module.
How do you prevent subclassing?
Raise an error in __init_subclass__() or use a metaclass.
What is cooperative multiple inheritance?
All classes use super() properly to ensure each method in chain gets called once.
How do you find all classes in hierarchy?
Use Class.__mro__ or walk through __bases__ recursively.
What is __str__ vs __repr__?
__str__ returns user-friendly string. __repr__ returns detailed, evaluable representation.
When is __str__ called?
__str__ is called by str() and print().
When is __repr__ called?
__repr__ is called by repr() and in interactive shell.
What is __format__?
__format__ customizes string formatting with format() and f-strings.
What is __eq__?
__eq__ enables the == operator.
What is __ne__?
__ne__ enables the != operator (defaults to not __eq__ if undefined).
What is __lt__?
__lt__ enables the < operator (less than).
What is __le__?
__le__ enables the <= operator (less than or equal).
What is __gt__?
__gt__ enables the > operator (greater than).
What is __ge__?
__ge__ enables the >= operator (greater than or equal).
What is @total_ordering?
@total_ordering auto-generates comparison methods from __eq__ and one other.
How do you implement safe equality?
Check isinstance() first, then compare attributes.
Can you compare different types?
Yes, but return False or NotImplemented if types differ.
What is __hash__?
__hash__ returns a hash value, enabling use as dict keys or in sets.
Why implement __hash__ with __eq__?
Equal objects must have equal hashes by Python contract.
What happens if you don't implement __hash__?
Instances become unhashable and can't be used in sets or dicts.
Can __hash__ change?
No, it must be consistent for the object's lifetime.
What is __bool__?
__bool__ defines truthiness, returning True or False.
What is the default for __bool__?
If undefined, __len__ is used (non-zero = True). Otherwise, True.
Can __bool__ return non-boolean?
Technically yes, but it's coerced to bool.
What is __add__?
__add__ enables the + operator.
What is __sub__?
__sub__ enables the - operator.
What is __mul__?
__mul__ enables the * operator.
What is __truediv__?
__truediv__ enables the / operator.
What is __floordiv__?
__floordiv__ enables the // operator.
What is __mod__?
__mod__ enables the % operator.
What is __pow__?
__pow__ enables the ** operator.
What is __radd__?
__radd__ enables addition when object is on right (a + obj).
What is __rsub__?
__rsub__ enables subtraction when object is on right.
What is __rmul__?
__rmul__ enables multiplication when object is on right.
What is __len__?
__len__ returns the length, enabling len().
What is __getitem__?
__getitem__ enables indexing with [].
What is __setitem__?
__setitem__ enables assignment via [].
What is __delitem__?
__delitem__ enables deletion via del.
What is __contains__?
__contains__ enables the 'in' operator.
What is __iter__?
__iter__ returns an iterator for for loops.
What is __next__?
__next__ returns the next value or raises StopIteration.
What is __reversed__?
__reversed__ enables reversed().
What is __call__?
__call__ makes instances callable like functions.
What is __index__?
__index__ allows objects to be used as indices.
What is @property?
@property lets you define methods accessed like attributes.
How do you use @property with @setter?
@property defines getter; @property_name.setter defines setter.
What is a read-only property?
A property with only @property decorator and no setter.
What is a computed property?
A property that calculates its value based on other attributes.
Can properties raise exceptions?
Yes, both getters and setters can raise exceptions.
How do you validate in property setters?
Check the value and raise ValueError for invalid inputs.
What is property caching?
Computing the value once and storing it for future access.
How do you make a lazy property?
Compute value on first access and cache it.
Can you override a property in a subclass?
Yes, redefine with @property in the child class.
What is @property.deleter?
@property_name.deleter defines behavior for del obj.property.
Can you have properties without setters?
Yes, they're read-only.
What is the performance impact of properties?
Minimal; they're as fast as regular attribute access.
How do you document properties?
Add docstrings to the property getter function.
Can you use @property on a classmethod?
No, they're incompatible descriptors.
How do you make a property thread-safe?
Use locks in the property getter and setter.
What is @classmethod?
@classmethod receives cls (the class) as first argument.
When do you use @classmethod?
For factory methods or operations on class-level data.
What is @staticmethod?
@staticmethod doesn't receive cls or self.
When do you use @staticmethod?
For utility functions logically grouped with the class.
Can you call @classmethod from an instance?
Yes, Python passes the class, not the instance.
How do classmethods help with subclassing?
They receive the actual subclass, enabling proper instantiation.
Can a classmethod call an instance method?
No, classmethods don't have access to instances.
Can a staticmethod call an instance method?
No, staticmethods have no access to instances.
What is a factory method?
A @classmethod that creates instances with alternative logic.
Can you override a staticmethod?
Yes, subclasses can override staticmethods.
How do you debug classmethods?
Print cls to see which class called the method.
Can you combine @property with @classmethod?
No, they're incompatible.
When should you use classmethod vs instance method?
classmethod for class-level operations, instance methods for object-level.
How do you make a class method from a regular method?
Use @classmethod decorator and change first parameter to cls.
Can staticmethods access class variables?
Only via ClassName.variable, not through the static method.
What is an abstract class?
A class defining an interface that subclasses must implement.
How do you create an abstract class?
Use abc module with ABC base and @abstractmethod decorator.
What is @abstractmethod?
A decorator marking methods that subclasses must implement.
What happens if you don't implement an abstract method?
Instantiation fails with TypeError.
Can abstract classes have concrete methods?
Yes, both concrete and abstract methods are allowed.
What is @abstractproperty?
@property with @abstractmethod for abstract properties.
Can you instantiate an abstract class?
No, even if all abstract methods are implemented.
How do you check if a class is abstract?
Check __abstractmethods__ attribute.
Can abstract classes have __init__?
Yes, but subclasses should call super().__init__().
What is the purpose of abstract classes?
They define interfaces and enforce implementation contracts.
Can you mix abstract and concrete methods?
Yes, both are allowed in abstract classes.
How do you inherit from two abstract classes?
You must implement all abstract methods from both.
Can abstract classes have class variables?
Yes, just regular class attributes.
What is @abstractclassmethod?
Deprecated; use @classmethod with @abstractmethod instead.
How do you force subclasses to override __init__?
Use @abstractmethod in the parent's __init__.
What is @dataclass?
@dataclass auto-generates __init__, __repr__, __eq__.
How do you specify defaults in dataclasses?
Use default= or default_factory in field().
What is __post_init__?
__post_init__ is called after __init__ for validation.
How do you make a dataclass immutable?
Use frozen=True.
Can dataclasses use inheritance?
Yes, but defaults must come after non-defaults.
What is field(init=False)?
Excludes a field from __init__.
What is field(repr=False)?
Excludes a field from __repr__.
What is field(compare=False)?
Excludes a field from equality comparisons.
What is field(hash=False)?
Excludes a field from __hash__.
What is field(metadata)?
Attach arbitrary metadata to a field.
Can dataclasses have methods?
Yes, define methods like in regular classes.
What does order=True do?
Generates comparison methods like __lt__, __le__.
How do you customize dataclass equality?
Define a custom __eq__ after @dataclass.
How do you copy a dataclass instance?
Use copy.copy() or copy.deepcopy().
What is the difference between dataclass and namedtuple?
dataclasses are mutable by default; namedtuples are immutable.
What is a decorator?
A function wrapping another function to modify its behavior.
How do you write a basic decorator?
Create a function that takes a function, wraps it, returns the wrapper.
How do you write a decorator with arguments?
Nest decorators: outer takes args, middle takes function, inner wraps it.
What is functools.wraps?
functools.wraps copies metadata from original function to wrapper.
How do you stack decorators?
Place multiple @decorator lines; they apply bottom-to-top.
How do you decorate a method?
Use decorator; wrapper must accept self.
How do you decorate a classmethod?
@classmethod should be outermost.
How do you decorate a staticmethod?
@staticmethod should be outermost.
How do you write a caching decorator?
Use a dictionary to cache function results.
How do you write a timing decorator?
Use time module to measure execution duration.
What is a decorator class?
A class with __call__ that acts as a decorator.
Can decorators modify function arguments?
Yes, the wrapper can pre-process arguments.
How do you write a retry decorator?
Use a loop in the wrapper to retry on exception.
Can you combine decorators with generators?
Yes, decorators can wrap generator functions.
How do you preserve function signature?
Use @wraps or functools.wraps.
What is a context manager?
An object handling setup and teardown via __enter__ and __exit__.
How do you use a context manager?
Use the 'with' statement to create a context.
What do __enter__ and __exit__ do?
__enter__ sets up resources; __exit__ handles cleanup.
How do you implement @contextmanager?
@contextmanager simplifies creation with yield.
How do you handle exceptions in __exit__?
Return True to suppress; False to propagate.
Can you use multiple context managers?
Yes, use comma-separated managers or Python 3.10+ parentheses.
What is the purpose of context managers?
Ensure resources are properly acquired and released.
How do you create a locking context manager?
Use lock in __enter__; release in __exit__.
Can context managers be nested?
Yes, nest with statements.
What if __enter__ raises an exception?
__exit__ is not called.
Can __exit__ modify exceptions?
Yes, you can transform or suppress exceptions.
How do you debug context managers?
Add print statements in __enter__ and __exit__.
What happens after with block exits?
__exit__ is called, even with exceptions.
Can you yield multiple times in @contextmanager?
No, @contextmanager should yield exactly once.
What is the difference from try/finally?
Context managers are cleaner and more readable.
What is a generator?
A function yielding values one at a time, producing an iterator.
How do you create a generator?
Use yield instead of return.
How does yield differ from return?
yield pauses and resumes; return ends execution.
What is a generator expression?
Syntax like list comprehension but with parentheses for lazy evaluation.
What does yield from do?
yield from delegates to another generator.
How do you send values to a generator?
Use send() to inject values; they become yield results.
What is the difference from list comprehension?
Generators are lazy; list comprehensions compute all upfront.
How do you convert a generator to a list?
Use list() to consume the generator.
Can generators be used with for loops?
Yes, generators are iterables.
How do you chain generators?
Use yield from or nest them.
How do you implement an infinite generator?
Use while True with yield.
What is a generator pipeline?
Chaining generators to process data.
What is the performance benefit?
Memory efficient; values computed on demand.
Can generators be pickled?
No, generators cannot be serialized.
What happens at the end of a generator?
StopIteration is raised automatically.
What is an iterable?
An object with __iter__() returning an iterator.
What is an iterator?
An object with __iter__() and __next__().
How do you implement a custom iterator?
Implement __iter__() and __next__().
What does StopIteration do?
Signals the end of iteration in __next__().
Can you use iter() on any object?
Only on objects with __iter__().
How do you make a reverse iterator?
Implement __reversed__().
What is the iter() function?
Returns an iterator from an iterable.
Can you call iter() twice on the same object?
Yes, each call returns a new iterator.
What happens if you call next() on a non-iterator?
TypeError is raised.
How do you make an iterable that supports slicing?
Implement __getitem__() with slice support.
Can you iterate over a class instance?
Yes, if it implements __iter__().
What is the relationship with for loops?
For loops automatically call iter() and next().
How do you make a range-like class?
Implement __iter__() and __getitem__().
What is the iterator protocol?
Objects implement __iter__() and __next__() for iteration.
Can generators be called multiple times?
No, exhausted generators cannot be restarted.
What is a metaclass?
A class of a class; classes are created from metaclasses.
How do you create a custom metaclass?
Inherit from type; override __new__ or __init__.
What are metaclass __new__ parameters?
mcs (metaclass), name, bases, dct (attributes).
How do you enforce class rules?
Override __new__ or __init__ to validate or modify classes.
Can you use multiple metaclasses?
Yes, but they must be compatible.
What is a metaclass conflict?
When parent metaclasses are incompatible.
How do you debug metaclasses?
Print in __new__ to trace class creation.
What is __init_subclass__()?
Called when a subclass is created; useful for enforcing rules.
Can metaclasses modify class methods?
Yes, they can add or modify any class attributes.
What is the use of metaclasses?
Control class creation and enforce patterns.
Can metaclasses prevent instantiation?
Yes, via __call__() in the metaclass.
What is a metaclass factory?
A metaclass that creates other metaclasses.
How do you use metaclasses with decorators?
They're independent; use both together for powerful patterns.
Can metaclasses have __init_subclass__()?
No, that's for regular classes.
What is the relationship with inheritance?
Metaclasses define how classes are created; inheritance defines class hierarchy.
What is a descriptor?
An object defining attribute access via __get__, __set__, __delete__.
What is __get__?
__get__ handles attribute reading.
What is __set__?
__set__ handles attribute assignment.
What is __delete__?
__delete__ handles attribute deletion.
What is a data descriptor?
A descriptor with __get__ and (__set__ or __delete__).
What is a non-data descriptor?
A descriptor with only __get__.
How does property use descriptors?
@property is implemented as a descriptor.
How do you create a validating descriptor?
Implement __set__() to validate before storing.
What is the descriptor protocol?
The mechanism for implementing custom attribute access.
How do you use descriptors in a class?
Assign descriptor instances to class attributes.
What is the descriptor lookup order?
Data descriptors, instance __dict__, non-data descriptors.
Can descriptors work with inheritance?
Yes, subclasses inherit descriptor behavior.
How do you make a lazy descriptor?
Store computation result on first access.
Can descriptors raise exceptions?
Yes, any method can raise exceptions.
How do you debug descriptors?
Add print in __get__, __set__, __delete__.
How do you do multiple inheritance?
List multiple parent classes separated by commas.
What is the diamond problem?
A class inherits from two parents sharing a common ancestor.
How does Python solve it?
Using C3 linearization in MRO.
What is C3 linearization?
An algorithm ensuring each class appears once in MRO.
How do you view MRO?
Use Class.mro() or Class.__mro__.
Can super() work with multiple inheritance?
Yes, super() follows MRO for cooperative inheritance.
What is cooperative multiple inheritance?
All classes use super() to ensure each method is called once.
How many parents can a class have?
Unlimited, but complexity increases.
What is the correct parent order?
Most specific to most general (left to right).
Can methods from different parents conflict?
Yes, MRO determines which is used.
How do you call a specific parent method?
Use ParentClass.method(self) or follow MRO with super().
What happens with __init__ in multiple inheritance?
Only the first parent's is called unless you use super().
Can you have circular inheritance?
No, Python prevents circular inheritance.
What is the mixin pattern?
Using multiple inheritance to add functionality.
How do you test multiple inheritance?
Test each inheritance path separately.
What is composition?
Using objects as attributes (has-a) rather than inheritance (is-a).
How does composition differ from inheritance?
Composition is more flexible; inheritance creates rigid hierarchies.
What is the Template Method pattern?
Base class defines structure; subclasses override specific steps.
What is a mixin class?
A class providing functionality combined via multiple inheritance.
What is the Singleton pattern?
Ensures only one instance of a class exists.
How do you implement Singleton?
Use __new__() or a metaclass to control instantiation.
What is the Factory pattern?
Using methods to create objects instead of direct instantiation.
What is the Observer pattern?
Objects notify multiple observers when state changes.
What is the Strategy pattern?
Encapsulate interchangeable behaviors as classes.
What is duck typing?
If it walks like a duck, it's a duck. Type-checking via behavior.
What is monkey patching?
Modifying classes or modules at runtime.
Should you use monkey patching?
Avoid in production; mainly for testing.
What is method chaining?
Calling methods on results of previous methods.
How do you implement method chaining?
Return self from methods.
What is lazy initialization?
Defer expensive operations until first access.
How do lazy properties work?
Compute and cache value on first access via @property.
What is the Adapter pattern?
Make incompatible interfaces work together by adapting one to the other.
What is the Decorator design pattern?
Wrap objects to add functionality dynamically without modifying the original.
What is the Builder pattern?
Construct complex objects step by step using a builder object.
What is the Facade pattern?
Provide a simplified interface to a complex subsystem.
What is the Proxy pattern?
Control access to another object by using a placeholder or surrogate.
What is the State pattern?
Allow objects to change behavior based on internal state changes.
What is the Chain of Responsibility?
Pass a request along a chain of handlers until one handles it.
What is the Command pattern?
Encapsulate requests as objects, enabling parameterization and queuing.
What is the Visitor pattern?
Define new operations on objects without changing their structure.
What is the Mediator pattern?
Define an object that encapsulates how a set of objects interact.
How do you use __getattr__ for dynamic attributes?
__getattr__ is called when an attribute isn't found; return a value or raise AttributeError.
What is __getattribute__ vs __getattr__?
__getattribute__ is called for every access; __getattr__ is only for missing attributes.
How do you intercept attribute setting?
Implement __setattr__() to intercept all attribute assignments.
How do you intercept attribute deletion?
Implement __delattr__() to intercept all attribute deletions.
What is __new__ vs __init__?
__new__ creates the instance; __init__ initializes it. Use __new__ for immutable types.
How do you override __new__ for immutables?
Override __new__ to validate and create the instance since __init__ can't modify immutables.
What is __subclasscheck__?
__subclasscheck__ in a metaclass customizes issubclass() behavior.
What is __instancecheck__?
__instancecheck__ in a metaclass customizes isinstance() behavior.
What is __reduce__?
__reduce__ is used for pickling; return a tuple describing how to recreate the object.
What is __reduce_ex__?
__reduce_ex__ is an extended version of __reduce__ used by pickle protocol versions.
How do you make a class pickleable?
Implement __getstate__() and __setstate__() or __reduce__().
What is __copy__?
__copy__ defines behavior when copy.copy() is called on an instance.
What is __deepcopy__?
__deepcopy__ defines behavior when copy.deepcopy() is called.
What is __sizeof__?
__sizeof__ returns the size in bytes of an object instance.
What is __fspath__?
__fspath__ enables using an object as a file system path.
What is __enter__ and __exit__?
__enter__ sets up context; __exit__ cleans up, even with exceptions.
What is __aenter__ and __aexit__?
__aenter__ and __aexit__ are async versions for async with statements.
What is __aiter__ and __anext__?
__aiter__ returns async iterator; __anext__ returns next value asynchronously.
What is __missing__?
__missing__ in dict subclasses is called for missing keys.
How do you make an attribute read-only after __init__?
Use __setattr__() to prevent modification after initialization.
How do you implement a property that validates on set?
Define setter to check value before assignment; raise ValueError if invalid.
What is a descriptor vs property?
Descriptors are the general mechanism; properties are a convenient descriptor implementation.
How do you create a cached property?
Compute value once, cache it in instance __dict__ or a separate cache.
What is functools.cached_property?
A decorator for properties that cache their value after first computation.
How do you inspect class structure?
Use dir(), vars(), getmembers() from inspect, or __dict__ attributes.
What is vars()?
vars() returns the __dict__ attribute of an object or module.
What is dir()?
dir() lists names in the current scope or attributes of an object.
What is isinstance() used for?
isinstance(obj, Class) checks if obj is an instance of Class or subclass.
What is type()?
type(obj) returns the class of an object; type(name, bases, dict) creates a class.
Can you dynamically create classes?
Yes, use type(name, bases, dict) or a metaclass.
What is __name__ vs __qualname__?
__name__ is simple name; __qualname__ includes enclosing classes/functions.
What is __module__?
__module__ contains the module name where a class is defined.
How do you check if something is callable?
Use callable(obj) to check if obj has __call__.
What is hasattr()?
hasattr(obj, name) checks if obj has an attribute named name.
What is getattr()?
getattr(obj, name, default) gets an attribute value with optional default.
What is setattr()?
setattr(obj, name, value) sets an attribute value dynamically.
What is delattr()?
delattr(obj, name) deletes an attribute dynamically.
How do you prevent attribute access?
Override __getattribute__() to raise AttributeError for forbidden attributes.
What is __all__?
__all__ defines which names are exported by from module import *.
How do you document classes?
Use docstrings immediately after class definition; access via __doc__.
What is PEP 8?
Python Enhancement Proposal 8 defines style guidelines for Python code.
What is typing hints?
Type hints annotate function arguments and returns for static analysis.
How do you use @overload?
@overload from typing defines multiple function signatures for the same function.
What is Protocol in typing?
Protocol defines structural typing for duck typing with type hints.
How do you enforce immutability?
Use frozen=True in @dataclass or @slots__() with __setattr__.
What is a namedtuple?
A lightweight immutable tuple subclass with named fields.
How does namedtuple differ from dataclass?
namedtuples are immutable and lightweight; dataclasses are mutable and flexible.
What is typing.NamedTuple?
A typed version of namedtuple with type hints.
What is attrs library?
An alternative to dataclasses with more features and flexibility.
How do you use @attr.s?
@attr.s is attrs equivalent of @dataclass for class definition.
What is @attr.define?
@attr.define is a modern attrs syntax equivalent to @dataclass.
What is weak reference?
A reference that doesn't prevent garbage collection; use weakref module.
When do you use weak references?
To avoid circular references and memory leaks.
What is __del__ used for?
__del__ is the destructor; use it for cleanup when objects are destroyed.
Is __del__ reliable?
No, __del__ timing is unpredictable. Use context managers instead.
What is garbage collection?
Automatic memory management that frees objects no longer referenced.
How do you detect circular references?
Use gc.get_referents() or gc.garbage after enabling debug mode.
What is gc.collect()?
Explicitly triggers garbage collection to free circular references.
Can you prevent garbage collection?
Yes, call gc.disable() but it's generally not recommended.
What is memory profiling?
Analyzing memory usage of Python programs using tools like memory_profiler.
How do you find memory leaks?
Use memory_profiler, objgraph, or sys.getsizeof() to track memory growth.
What is repr() vs str()?
repr() calls __repr__ (for debugging); str() calls __str__ (for users).
How do you write good __repr__?
Return a string that eval() can use to recreate the object if possible.
What is f-string with !r?
f'{obj!r}' calls repr() on obj in the f-string.
What is f-string with !s?
f'{obj!s}' calls str() on obj in the f-string.
What is f-string with !a?
f'{obj!a}' calls ascii() on obj in the f-string.
How do you implement __format__ for custom formatting?
Define __format__(self, format_spec) to return formatted string.
What is format specification mini-language?
Syntax for format strings like f'{value:format_spec}'.
Can you use __slots__ with properties?
Yes, properties work fine with __slots__.
Can you use __slots__ with __dict__?
Yes, add '__dict__' to __slots__ to allow extra attributes.
Can you use __slots__ with weakref?
Yes, add '__weakref__' to __slots__ to support weak references.
What is functools.total_ordering?
@total_ordering generates comparison methods from __eq__ and one other.
What is functools.partial?
functools.partial creates a partial function with fixed arguments.
What is functools.lru_cache?
@lru_cache caches function results based on arguments.
What is functools.wraps?
@wraps preserves original function metadata in decorators.
What is inspect module?
inspect provides tools for introspecting objects: signature(), getsource(), etc.
What is inspect.signature()?
Returns a Signature object describing function parameters.
What is inspect.getsource()?
Returns the source code of a class or function as a string.
What is inspect.getmembers()?
Returns a list of (name, value) tuples for object members.
What is __annotations__?
__annotations__ is a dict of type hints for a function or class.
How do you read annotations at runtime?
Access function.__annotations__ or class.__annotations__ dictionary.
What is typing.get_type_hints()?
Returns a dict of type hints with forward references resolved.
Can you use typing hints with inheritance?
Yes, subclasses can override parent type hints.
What is variance in type hints?
Covariance/contravariance describe how type hierarchies translate to generic types.
What is Protocol vs ABC?
Protocol uses structural typing (duck typing); ABC uses nominal typing (inheritance).
How do you combine Protocol with @runtime_checkable?
@runtime_checkable allows isinstance() checks with Protocol.
What is typing.Final?
typing.Final marks a variable as not intended to be reassigned.
What is typing.Literal?
typing.Literal restricts a type to specific literal values.
What is typing.TypedDict?
TypedDict creates a type-hinted dictionary with specific keys.
What is typing.Generic?
Generic allows creating generic classes with type parameters.
How do you use TypeVar with Generic?
Define TypeVar('T'), inherit Generic[T] to create a generic class.
What is typing.ClassVar?
ClassVar marks a variable as a class attribute in type hints.
What is typing.Optional?
Optional[T] is equivalent to Union[T, None] for nullable types.
What is typing.Union?
Union[A, B] means the type is either A or B.
What is typing.Any?
Any disables type checking for a variable; use sparingly.
Can decorators preserve type hints?
Yes, use functools.wraps to preserve __annotations__.
What is __post_init__ in dataclass with fields?
__post_init__ can access field values to perform validation or setup.
How do you make a dataclass with only some fields hashable?
Use field(hash=False) for fields to exclude from __hash__.
What is field(kw_only=True)?
field(kw_only=True) makes that field keyword-only in __init__.
What is field(metadata)?
Attach arbitrary metadata to a field for custom processing.
Can you use fields() to inspect dataclass fields?
Yes, fields() returns a tuple of Field objects describing the dataclass.
What is is_dataclass()?
is_dataclass(obj) checks if obj is a dataclass or instance.
What is asdict() for dataclasses?
asdict() converts a dataclass instance to a dictionary.
What is astuple() for dataclasses?
astuple() converts a dataclass instance to a tuple.
Can dataclasses inherit from non-dataclasses?
Yes, but the parent must not have __init__ or you should call super().__init__().
What is the enum.Enum?
A class with fixed enum members accessed as attributes.
What is enum.IntEnum?
An Enum subclass where members are integers and support comparison.
What is enum.Flag?
An Enum subclass supporting bitwise operations on members.
What is enum.IntFlag?
A combination of IntEnum and Flag for integer flag enums.
How do you iterate over enum members?
Use for member in EnumClass: to iterate all enum members.
How do you access enum members?
Use EnumClass.MEMBER or EnumClass['MEMBER'] or EnumClass(value).
What is enum.auto()
auto() automatically generates sequential values for enum members.
Can enums have methods?
Yes, define methods in the Enum class like any other class.
What is enum value checking?
isinstance(obj, Enum) checks if obj is any enum member.
How do you get enum name from value?
Use EnumClass(value).name to get the name of an enum member by value.
What is comparison in enums?
Enum members support == and != but not < or > unless IntEnum or Flag.
What is _missing_ hook?
Define _missing_() in Enum to handle lookup of undefined values.
What is _order_ in enums?
_order_ is a string defining enum member order (Python 3.10+).
Can you subclass enums?
Yes, but a derived enum can't have both members and non-member attributes.
What is __init_subclass__ hook?
__init_subclass__() is called when a subclass is created; useful for enforcement.
How do you use __init_subclass__?
Define __init_subclass__() in a class to validate subclass creation.
What is __set_name__?
__set_name__() in descriptors is called when attached to a class, receiving the attribute name.
When is __set_name__ called?
__set_name__() is called during class creation, after class body execution.
How do you use __set_name__ in descriptors?
Store the attribute name in __set_name__() for debugging and validation.
What is @classmethod vs @classmethod factory?
@classmethod enables alternative constructors that return instances of the class.
How do you make a class immutable?
Use frozen=True in dataclass or override __setattr__ to raise FrozenInstanceError.
What is FrozenInstanceError?
An error raised when attempting to modify a frozen dataclass instance.
How do you document magic methods?
Add docstrings to magic methods like any other method for IDE support.
